rules.statement: A setting the role cannot change is shown disabled with the reason and the role that can change it; hiding it makes the product look broken and invites support tickets.
Unsaved changes are visible without scrolling: the save bar appears, the page warns on navigation, and the count of changed fields is announced.
Saving disables the button on press, guards the handler, and sends an idempotency key so a double submit or a retry cannot apply the change twice.
A toggle that takes effect on save says so next to the control; a toggle that applies immediately shows its pending state until the server confirms.
A failed save keeps every edited value in place, names which field failed and why, and offers a retry that reuses the same idempotency key.
Destructive settings (delete workspace, revoke all sessions) live in their own section, carry the typed confirmation the action deserves, and never share a save button with reversible ones.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a save response applies only to the local revision it was sent for; edits made while the request was in flight keep the page dirty instead of being marked saved

sections.intent: Let one person change how their workspace behaves, know exactly what has been saved, and recover from a failed save without retyping.
useCases: revoke every session after a laptop is lost
nicheDifferences: Settings are visited rarely and changed nervously: the cost of a wrong click is a workspace-wide consequence
Certainty therefore outranks brevity, and every irreversible action is separated from the reversible ones
